Jack Zhao and I built Lazarus to help founders & GTM teams find revenue problems earlier and act on them faster, for Y Combinator 's First-Ever Growth Hackathon! The idea is simple: most outbound today starts with a generic list and a generic message. The Lazarus starts with a signal. It helps teams identify companies or customer segments that may be showing signs of distress, diagnose what might be going wrong, and turn that into a clearer, more useful outreach motion. https://lnkd.in/gQ5QeVfd Using metric backend GTM strategy, we find the right people, and help set your ideas in motion so you can get backed to building. #GTM #GrowthEngineering #AI #RevenueOperations #YCHackathon

Today we’re launching Meridian, the AI platform for accounting firms that runs the month-end close from start to finish. We’ve used it to close 187,000 months of books for more than 8,000 clients, and we’re excited to now make it available for other firms. With Meridian, you don’t need to learn complicated tools or babysit agents doing microtasks. Just connect your client’s GL, upload any supporting documents, and it handles the rest: executing the complete close according to your firm’s policies and client-specific processes. Your team reviews the finished financials. You can also delegate complex projects and client support tasks to Meridian via a simple chat interface. Accounting has historically been a tough mix of satisfying, skillful work and important but tedious mechanical work. I love how much of the grind Meridian removes for the team, freeing them up to do the work they most enjoy doing. An urgent need for years of restated financials is no sweat – done and reviewed in a few hours. Gnarly client support questions are addressed with the infinite patience of an AI agent. An autonomous close is a predictable close that is always delivered on time. An autonomous close also helps firms reimagine their structure and economics in important ways. It’s easier to do more for clients, who see what AI can do and are expecting more. It’s easier to attract, reward, and retain the best accounting talent. It’s easier to grow. I personally maintain a $500k revenue portfolio on Meridian to stay close to the tech, while I watch TV in the evenings after my kids go to bed. It’s wild that that’s even possible, and it keeps getting better. I’d love for you to check it out and let me know what you think. Learn more at meridian.pilot.com .

I'm thankful for the opportunity this past weekend to represent Lehigh Aerial Swarms at RoboConn at Columbia University! It was great to be able to show off our autonomous blimps and connect with other robotics clubs, organizations, and companies across the Northeast. Thank you to the Columbia University Robotics Club for putting together such an inspiring event. Looking forward to getting back in the lab to prepare for our competition this November!

Thrilled to have represented Lehigh Aerial Swarms at RoboCONN this past weekend at Columbia University! With David Cai Liang , Jacob Booser , Sijie Wang , @Ray Jing, Yusong Bai , Andrew Dai & Juan Carlos Tique Rangel . Our team had the opportunity to demo our autonomous blimps, connect with robotics clubs and organizations across the Northeast, and engage with industry professionals. It was especially exciting to showcase how we’re building lighter-than-air swarm robots, from hardware assembly to implementing control systems like state machines and PID for autonomous object detection. Aerial Swarms is all about pushing the boundaries of swarm robotics through hands-on innovation, and it was incredible to share that work with such a passionate community. A big thank you to our advisor David Saldana, the Lehigh CSE Department, and the P.C. Rossin College of Engineering and Applied Science at Lehigh University for supporting our trip and enabling us to showcase our work. Excited to bring this momentum back to the lab as we prepare for competition this November 🚀 #Robotics #SwarmRobotics #Engineering #Innovation #LehighUniversity #AerialSwarms #RoboCONN

I'm grateful to have had the opportunity to attend the Liberty Intern Talent Summit in Boston as a Full-Stack Software Engineering Intern in the Liberty Mutual Insurance TechStart program, marking the halfway point of my internship. Throughout the summit, I connected with over 200 fellow interns, attended professional development workshops, toured the Boston office, and asked Tim Sweeney and Melanie Foley about their careers as executive leaders during keynote and AMA sessions. These conversations gave me a deeper appreciation for Liberty Mutual's culture and the breadth of work happening across the organization. Thank you to everyone who made this experience so memorable, especially the Early Talent team for their thoughtful organization and dedication in bringing it all together. I’m leaving the summit feeling energized from the events, grateful for the relationships I’ve built, and excited to carry that momentum into the rest of my internship. (Also, I did not expect to end up singing on stage in front of 200 interns, but here we are!) #WorkAtLiberty #LIT2026 #LibertyMutual 🗽

Wrapping up a very eventful week! From Monday to Thursday, I had the opportunity to attend TechDevCon in New York City, where I was not only able to connect with my intern cohort but also hear from guest speakers representing Microsoft, Bloomberg, J.P. Morgan, Forter, Capital One, and more, along with changemakers making a real impact in their communities. I want to start by thanking many of our incredible speakers and guests: Jameelah Calhoun , David L. Jackson , Segun Akinyemi , Peter Conroy , Gregory Ugwi , Benita Besa , Manyaka A. , and so many more, for their wonderful presentations. We covered everything from whether tech jobs are actually "cooked" because of AI (spoiler: not that cooked), to all the AI engineering buzzwords from context engineering to graph engineering and whatever the next trend will be a month from now, and even had heartfelt conversations about building genuine connections in tech. A huge thank you to SEO (Sponsors for Educational Opportunity) for putting this all together! Special shoutout to Erica Wong , Jake Son , and the rest of the SEO TechDev staff working behind the scenes. I know it can't be easy coordinating everything for 100+ students each week while making sure every one of us is set up for success throughout the summer program and beyond. Most definitely have to shout out my manager David N. for all the lessons he shared throughout the program. I'm truly grateful for the advice, guidance, and time you invested in our group. Speaking of our group, I want to give a huge thank you to Adesola O. Edgar Agramonte Victoria Agyare Crystal Low Rafael Emilio Arte-Suriel Ashfin Rahman James Butts for making our Zoom meetings feel like a little community. You all made the experience that much more enjoyable.

Yesterday marked the end of my 11-week co-op with Alaska Airlines on the Avionics Engineering team! ✈️ Over the summer, I had the opportunity to develop Task Cards—aircraft maintenance work instructions—using the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM) and Standard Wiring Practices Manual (SWPM). This experience strengthened my technical writing, problem-solving, and engineering skills while providing valuable insight into the commercial aviation industry. I am incredibly grateful to the entire Avionics Engineering team and my manager Stephanie Gardner for their guidance, support, and mentorship throughout the summer. I also want to give a shoutout to the fellow interns and co-ops I had the pleasure of working alongside in the Seattle hangar: Arvind Sthanukrishnan , Mihir V. , my fellow Lehigh peer Lucas Koranda , John Knobbe , and Adrienne McNeil . From exploring Seattle to traveling across the country with Alaska Airlines , this summer was one I will never forget!

This summer, I helped build a new micro frontend application in React and TypeScript that will unify the user experience of two stakeholder groups. I am so grateful to implement new code, practice agile methodologies, and learn alongside a group of wonderful engineers, designers, and product owners. Outside of my day-to-day, I had lots of opportunities to delve into my career development by joining professional workshops, attending the Liberty Intern Talent Summit in Boston, and volunteering at Intern Giveback Day! I would love to give a special thanks to those who helped support my growth at Liberty Mutual, specifically Josh Ambrose , Kaiden Terrana , Kayla Marshall , Shiloh Munsen , and Angela C. ! 🫶 As I prepare for my upcoming graduation in December, I'm excited to explore what's next! #WorkAtLiberty
